allowedHistoricalReferences.sourceText: D33,Data,"AZ and NH ballot surfaces (S3, into S2's shape)","Pima County AZ (85701+85641) and Merrimack County NH (03255) ballots behind the BallotSource contract, with a per-state registry so the ballot follows the map. Same discipline as Morris County: authority documents as primary sources, candidates as filed, cited absences, alphabetical order stated, incumbency null (filings do not state it).",P0,Done,,,"2026-08-14, branch claude/restore-representation-session-0814 (second session). ARIZONA (data/ballot/az-pima-2026.json): transcribed from the SOS partisan candidate filing PDF (2026-Candidate-Nominations-and-Petitions-Filed-0330.pdf, text-extracted via pdfjs) - 12 candidacy contests worth of filings reduced to the 9-per-zip Pima view (6 statewide offices, CD-6/CD-7, LD-19/LD-20 senate+house, AZ two-reps-per-district carried as voteFor 2), 44 candidacies with party labels as filed. PRIMARY-STAGE HONESTY per the brief: the July 21 primary was canvassed Aug 6 (azsos event 955) but the SOS has not published a general-election candidate list, so every filed candidate renders with a computed scope note saying exactly that and when it narrows - never a news-reported winner (news names for the nominees exist but are not an election authority and were not used). Corporation Commission deliberately omitted: the filing does not state how many of five seats are scheduled; a guessed seat count is a claim (curator note + coverageNote). 11 statewide measures as MEASURE contests: Legislative Council short titles, each linked to the Council's ADOPTED IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS PDF on azleg.gov (three URLs probe-verified 200); official question text NOT claimed - the SOS publicity pamphlet is pending and the page says so (the verbatim-question rule stays intact). Cited absence: no U.S. Senate seat on AZ's 2026 ballot per the filing. NEW HAMPSHIRE (data/ballot/nh-merrimack-2026.json): transcribed from the SOS cumulative primary filing (cumulative-filings-7.16.26.pdf, both party sections; sos.nh.gov serves 403 to plain clients - fetched via the UA-sensitive-bot-wall ladder rung) - 10 contests for a Newbury voter (Governor, open US Senate with 13 filed and the Shaheen-not-running note, CD-2, State Senate 7, Merrimack County District 7 voteFor 2, five county offices from the MERRIMACK sections), 41 candidacies. THE NOVEMBER FINDING stated as the system working: town and school matters decide at the March town meeting - two cited absence rows (Newbury town, Kearsarge Regional) citing the SOS political calendar (Town Election: March 10, 2026). Executive Council + county-commissioner districts not in our geometry: stated in coverageNotes, never smoothed over. SHARED: BallotSet gained coverageNotes (our gaps, distinct from authority absences, rendered under NOT HERE YET); lib/sources/ballot-curated (factory over the shared validator); lib/ballot/registry.ts (page loops all sources - the ballot follows the map, 2e closes); covered-states now nj+az+nh with a test pinning it to the registry; AZ + NH dates strips in election-dates.ts from azsos.gov and the SOS political calendar. Gate: /ballot at phone width all four zips (ballot-<zip>-phone.png), citations probe-verified. Evidence: test 263 pass (5 new), lint clean, tsc clean, build exit 0. 2026-08-15 THE GENERAL LINEUP IS CERTIFIED (6a): data/ballot/az-general-lineup-2026.json renders each party's primary winner per the State of Arizona Official Canvass (the certified record; a scan read by page-image extraction, method recorded in the file's citation and the ladder). Filing-list fallback retired for the 12 lineup contests; primary-stage scopeNotes suppressed there. One divergence the canvass ruled on: filed Slawson (D, LD-19 senate) absent from the certified record - the nominee is write-in winner Bob Karp. The measures' official question text remains pending (publicity pamphlet). 2026-08-16 THE NOVEMBER FINDING CORRECTED IN PLACE (overturn preserved): the thin-November claim was true ONLY for town and school offices (March town meeting) - for state/federal offices NH 2026-11-03 [expected-future: general election day, R16] is one of the largest ballots in the country (governor two-year term, US Senate, both US House seats, all 24 state senate + 400 state house seats, Executive Council, county offices). The two contests the coverageNotes had parked as unmappable are now LISTED with filed candidates, keyed to Newbury town division on the SOS own 2022-2032 assignment documents: Executive Councilor District 2 (Liot Hill D; Menard, Strathdee R - 2022-2032-executive-council-districts.pdf places Newbury in D2) and Merrimack County Commissioner Second District, 2-year term elected 2026 (Ribas D; Bilodeau, French R - 2022-2032-county-commissioners-by-district_0.pdf). House district verified: Merrimack 7 = New London + Newbury, 2 seats, and NO floterial covers Newbury per 2022-2032-state-representative-and-delegate-districts.pdf - which corrects state.md 2 floterial claim for Newbury specifically. 03255 now renders 12 contests / 47 candidacies. Branch claude/nh-ballot-kelly-standard-0816; test 315 pass."

Ask about commercial-use terms in the first call.,P1,In progress,,,"2026-08-13 INVESTIGATED — docs/ballot-research-2026.md is the full report. Democracy Works Elections API: JSON, reaches sub-municipal but only jurisdictions over 5,000 people (Newbury ~2,200 falls under the floor — the gap sits exactly where our NH pins are), commercial licensing exists (TikTok/Perplexity/Nextdoor are partners), pricing by request. CTCL/BIP: nationwide candidate data, but direct access is for mission-aligned nonprofits and doubtful for a for-profit data seller; the realistic channel is the Google Civic Info API elections endpoints (still live — only Representatives was retired), free, 25k/day, per-address query-time, NOT a bulk feed, caching terms UNVERIFIED. VIP spec public; state feeds not public raw. NONE of AZ/NJ/NH publish ballot content machine-readably (portal/PDF everywhere); the only real adjacent feed is NJ ELEC campaign-finance CSV (verified). Conclusion for November: curation per jurisdiction, into the VIP-like shape the report describes. Status In progress because the first call (terms/pricing) has not been made — that is the author. 2026-08-14 THE FIRST BALLOT SHIPPED (S2), branch claude/restore-representation-session-0814: the Morris County ballot for 07866, curated from the clerk's own filed-candidate PDFs (general 080726 + school 072826b revisions) into data/ballot/nj-morris-2026.json behind a BallotSource contract (lib/ballot/types.ts) parallel to MeetingSource — fetch() reads the committed file, so the D08 national feed is a source swap later. Every contest a Rockaway Twp voter sees 2026-11-03 [expected-future: general election day, R16]: US Senate (4 candidates), US House NJ-11 (3), County Commissioner (2), Rockaway Twp BOE vote-for-2 + unexpired (4), Morris Hills Regional Rockaway seats (2) — plus the clerk's own NO LOCAL ELECTION statement and the no-statewide-question statement, both cited as absences. OCD-ID + vintage joins; /ballot?zip= renders server-side with the NJ date strip (registration Oct 13, VBM mails Sep 19, early voting Oct 24-Nov 1, all cited to the state timeline PDF) shaped for AZ/NH next. Neutrality: alphabetical order (the clerk's ballot-position drawing PDF is a scan with no text layer - recorded miss), incumbency null (the filing does not state it), no websites (not in the filing), guard tests extended to ballot shapes AND the committed JSON (tests/neutrality-guards.test.ts), transparency page gained the ballot sentence. tests/ballot.test.ts asserts the 07866 join with denominators and that an AZ zip matches nothing. Screenshot ballot-07866-phone.png. test 246 pass, lint clean, build exit 0. Still open on this row: the Democracy Works pricing call (author), and the AZ/NH ballots."

allowedHistoricalReferences.sourceText: P01,Core product,Plain-language measure explainer,"Decompose each measure into contested provisions - funding, program, oversight, sunset.",P1,Done,,,"2026-08-15 THE MEASURE EXPLAINER LAYER EXISTS (2b+4d): all 11 AZ measures render the Legislative Council analysis VERBATIM (fetched+extracted, data/ballot/az-analyses-2026.json) beneath a curated plain-language summary labeled ""read the official text below"", each summary cited to the exact analysis URL it summarizes (tests/measure-summaries.test.ts: citation resolution, no advocacy vocabulary, completeness both directions). STILL OPEN for this row: decomposition into contested provisions (funding/program/oversight/sunset) - summaries today are whole-measure; provisions are what reactions will attach to. || 2026-08-17 (g12). NOT REACHED - deferred whole with item 5's remainder, at 2 of 13. Decomposition into contested provisions (funding / program / oversight / sunset) is still the open half, and it is still what P03's measure reactions attach to, so the two remain in that order.|| 2026-08-18 (g16, branch claude/g16-deploy-leaks-queue-0818). THE OPEN HALF IS BUILT: all 11 AZ measures are decomposed into contested provisions, 52 of them, at lib/ballot/measure-provisions.ts, rendered on the ballot page between the plain-language summary and the official analysis. THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL'S OWN ENUMERATION, not ours: where the adopted analysis numbers the parts, those numbers are the provisions. Nothing is split finer than the official text splits it and nothing is merged that it kept apart - a provision boundary this product invented would be editorialising with a scalpel. THE SHAPE, measured rather than expected: FUNDING 10, PROGRAM 26, OVERSIGHT 12, SUNSET 4. Proposition 212 carries 11 provisions on its own; Proposition 141 carries 3 and has NO oversight and NO clock. NOT EVERY MEASURE HAS ALL FOUR KINDS AND THAT IS THE FINDING - manufacturing a funding provision for a measure that funds nothing would be inventing a claim about a real measure. ONE READING WAS WIDENED DELIBERATELY AND IS THE AUTHOR'S TO NARROW: SUNSET is read as the measure's CLOCK - when it starts, when it ends, when it must be renewed - because a strict expiry-only reading would leave Proposition 143's applies-beginning-January-1-2028 and Proposition 316's two-year freeze with no kind at all, while Proposition 319's ten-year re-approval cycle is a sunset in the strict sense. No fifth kind was added: the kinds are what reactions get bucketed by, and changing that bucketing is an ask-the-author change. AN UNENUMERATED CATCH-ALL IS NOT MADE INTO A PROVISION: Proposition 142's analysis ends 'would provide for specified exceptions' without listing them, and a provision reading 'there are exceptions and we do not know what they are' would be a reaction target attached to nothing; it stays in the verbatim text where the reader sees exactly as much as the state published. EVERY ID IS THE REACTION TARGET P03 WILL USE, shaped <contestId>#<slug> and stated in the module to be permanent - a renumbered id silently orphans every reaction already collected against it. A MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING because it is the class this repo has a rule about: the first draft HAND-TYPED the eleven analysis URLs and got SIX OF THEM WRONG. A plausible URL is not a URL. The citation is now READ OFF THE ANALYSIS RECORD the page already renders verbatim, and a contest with no record throws rather than getting an invented link. tests/measure-provisions.test.ts, 9 tests: both directions of completeness (no measure with an analysis left undecomposed, no provision without one) with the denominator stated at 11; every provision cites its own measure's analysis; provisions and the measure summary cite the SAME document; ids unique, shaped, and resolvable; kinds closed to the four with a reader-facing label that is never the enum; no advocacy vocabulary; no OCD-ID, contest id or enum value reaching a reader; labels that are names and not sentences; and the per-kind shape asserted as MEASURED. STILL OPEN AND IT IS P03's, not this row's: reactions attached to these provisions. The data layer is ready for it - every provision has a stable target id and the render already sits after the explanation, which is where CLAUDE.md requires the ask to be. test 1008 pass, tsc clean, lint 0 errors, allowlist 15 of 15.|| 2026-08-18 (g17, branch claude/g17-budgets-geo-cadence-0818). REOPENED AND CLOSED AGAIN ON RULING 7C: SUNSET NARROWS AND A FIFTH KIND IS NAMED. Kinds are the reaction bucketing, so a bucket meaning both ""does this expire"" and ""when does this start"" collects answers to two questions and reports them as one number. THE TWO ORPHANS UNDER THE NARROWED DEFINITION, verbatim and reported before any kind was proposed: prop-143#starts-2028 ""The measure would apply beginning January 1, 2028."" and prop-144#starts-2028 ""It would apply to all elections taking place on or after January 1, 2028."" Both cite the Legislative Council analysis, read off the analysis record rather than typed. THE NAME IS DERIVED FROM THEM: both say when the measure starts applying, so the kind is START, reader label ""When it starts"". It encodes no stance — a start date is neither good nor bad — and tests/measure-provisions.test.ts refuses a loaded or identifier-shaped label on any kind. ALL FOUR SUNSET ROWS RE-DERIVED, not just the orphans: TWO MOVED. The two that stay are prop-316#freeze-window, which ends on a stated date, and prop-319#ten-year-renewal, which is renewal in the strict sense — note this is a DIFFERENT pair from the one the pre-narrowing header named as orphans, and the re-derivation is why. Every non-SUNSET provision was re-read for the same shape; three carry dates and none moves, because in each the date qualifies a substantive rule rather than being the provision's subject. CENSUS, before and after side by side: FUNDING 10/10, PROGRAM 26/26, OVERSIGHT 12/12, SUNSET 4/2, START -/2, total 52/52. PROP 141 SURVIVES INTACT and it is asserted twice — on its kinds (FUNDING, PROGRAM, PROGRAM, and none of OVERSIGHT, SUNSET or START) and on the absence of any year in any of its three provisions, so a mis-kinded row cannot satisfy both halves by accident. THE NAME IS FLAGGED FOR THE AUTHOR: a rename costs nothing today because there is no real reaction history to split, and the cost rises the moment real users arrive. Evidence: test 1032 pass 0 fail, lint clean, tsc clean, build green; label verified rendered on /ballot at 85701 by screenshot, one line at the eyebrow size on a 430px viewport."

allowedHistoricalReferences.sourceText: HUNT04,Ballot,The 03255 candidate sweep - 47 candidacies to the Kelly standard,The h brief item 3. The frozen ballot universe is 12 contests and 47 candidacies; zero were hunted.,P0,Not started,HUNT01,,"2026-08-16 (h item 3). DEFERRED WHOLE. THE DENOMINATOR IS ALREADY FROZEN and that is the half that exists: the 2026 New Hampshire General Election (election id nh-2026-11-03 [expected-future: NH general polling day, per the SoS political calendar in data/ballot/nh-merrimack-2026.json, read 2026-08-14]), from the Secretary of State cumulative primary filing (cumulative-filings-7.16.26.pdf, July 16 revision) as transcribed into data/ballot/nh-merrimack-2026.json - 12 contests, 47 candidacies, 0 measures, and 03255 resolves to ONE ballot style rather than a union of several (Newbury sits wholly inside NH-2, State Senate 7, NH House Merrimack 7, Executive Council 2 and County Commissioner District 2). Full record in docs/universe-03255.md section 5. THE SPEC: hunt every one of the 47 to the same Kelly standard as officeholders under the same ladder, with equal effort RECORDED PER RACE. Victoria finding is standing product law - a thin card tracks incumbency and campaign professionalism rather than merit, so a hunt that stops when the well-covered candidates are done has produced a ranking. Where a candidate hunt comes back empty after the ladder is exhausted, the card says so with THIN_CANDIDATE_LINE and its rungs; a race is NEVER rendered with one full card and one blank. Photos under the four-door rule with the door recorded per person; campaign sites under the Facebook-as-campaign-site rule where the trail is establishable; blurbs carrying their source class. ONE CAVEAT BELONGS ON THE DENOMINATOR: these are PRIMARY filings and the September 8 2026 primary decides the general lineup, so the 47 are everyone who filed. Equal effort is owed across all 47 regardless - hunting only the likely survivors would be a prediction, and predictions are the thing this product does not do."

allowedHistoricalReferences.sourceText: M136,Map & UI,Body battlecards to person-card depth,The author: 'The battlecards should be the ultimate holy shit there is a ton of info in here.',P1,Done,,,"2026-08-16 (g4 item 10). DEFERRED WHOLE. THE SPEC, in the brief's own order, so nothing is lost: a body card carries, in the collapsible-section grammar — (1) IDENTITY: body name, tier/type chip row, jurisdiction; (2) WHAT THIS BODY DOES: plain-language role and powers, sourced; (3) REPRESENTATION: every seat held, each row opening that person's card, and school districts carry the SUPERINTENDENT (the author's earlier note, still not built) sourced like any other seat; (4) MEETINGS: item 11's ordering and pills, upcoming first — the ordering function now exists at lib/meetings/ordering.ts and is ready to use; (5) CONTACT: the pill row under item 8's rules, which now render both numbers labelled; (6) PLACES WITHIN / jurisdiction facts where held; (7) SOURCES, populated, per g2 item 1's assembler. Where something is not held, the HONEST ABSENCE LINE for that section — never an empty section, never a hidden one. DONE IS TESTABLE and the test is named in the brief: Pima (county), Tucson (municipal) and Tucson Unified (school) each render every applicable section with either content or an honest line, and the walk asserts it on all three. Blocked on nothing external. || 2026-08-17 (g12). DEFERRED WHOLE, never started - not thinned and not partially built. The session's brief ordered items 0 through 5 and was explicit that nothing in it was cuttable; the order was followed and the session ended inside item 5, having completed M134 and M93 of that item's thirteen rows. Under the deferral boundary this is reported as 2 of 13, not as a deferred sweep. The row's spec is unchanged and the seven sections, the honest absence line per section and the Pima / Tucson / Tucson Unified test are all still exactly what done means. ONE THING THIS SESSION CHANGED THAT THE NEXT BUILDER SHOULD KNOW: G05 rule 4e now puts the pill cluster at the top of the who-governs card, and rule 4c makes the rail, WGH and the large battlecard mutually exclusive on every reader-initiated open - so a body battlecard opening now CLOSES the surface it was opened from, and the card is the only thing on screen. That is more room than the spec assumed, not less. || 2026-08-18 (g13, branch claude/g13-final-rows-0818). DONE. test / lint / build pass; tsc --noEmit clean; 965 tests pass, 0 fail. THE SEVEN SECTIONS SHIPPED, in the collapsible grammar: (1) IDENTITY renders always-open above the sections - the header carries name, tier and jurisdiction and the fact rows qualify it; (2) WHAT THIS BODY DOES from the new lib/officials/body-blurbs.ts; (3) WHO SITS ON IT, every seat opening that person's card, with a school district's SUPERINTENDENT as its own labelled sub-block; (4) MEETINGS through lib/meetings/ordering.ts, upcoming first, with the upcoming count and the ordering read from ONE Date.now() so the header cannot disagree with the block; (5) CONTACT; (6) WHERE IT GOVERNS; (7) SOURCES. Sections and the tab strip are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE - a body card carrying both would say everything twice - so district and meeting cards keep their tabs untouched. EVERY SECTION RENDERS FOR EVERY BODY: an empty one collapses closed with its own honest absence line inside and its header visible, per the author's 2026-08-17 ruling on M93. Nothing is hidden for lack of content, and tests/body-battlecard.test.ts asserts the section set is never filtered - hiding empties would make a well-covered body's card taller than a thin one's, the same layout asymmetry the equal-effort rule catches. SECTION 2 IS SOURCED, NEVER GENERATED: three entries, each a plain-language paraphrase of a statute or charter READ on 2026-08-18 and cited with its URL - A.R.S. 11-251 (county board powers) for Pima, A.R.S. 15-341 (governing board; powers and duties) for Tucson Unified, and the Tucson City Charter's council-manager form for Tucson, which overrides any state-level municipal answer because a generic one would falsely say its council runs the city. There is deliberately NO national default: what a county board does differs in all fifty states, so a body with no read statute gets the honest line and no paraphrase. STATED GAP: New Hampshire's three governing classes (Merrimack County, Newbury, Kearsarge Regional) have no entry yet - they render the absence line, identically to every other unsourced body, until a session reads RSA 28, RSA 47 and RSA 189 the way this one read the Arizona statutes. Guarded by 8 tests in tests/body-battlecard.test.ts plus 6 new walk checks in scripts/walk-all.mts asserting all six section headers AND the absence of any internal identifier on Pima, Tucson and Tucson Unified - the row's own named done-test."

allowedHistoricalReferences.sourceText: M21,Map & UI,Link ladder and body coverage audit,"Every meeting gets somewhere to click, and a body nobody looked at stops being indistinguishable from one that was searched.",P0,Done,M16,,"2026-08-12, branch claude/link-ladder-and-coverage-audit. DONE: test (147 pass, 15 new in tests/link-ladder.test.ts), lint, tsc and build all green, verified on screen at 03255 and 85641 (screenshots/4610-newbury-popup.png, 4610-85641-coverage.png). TWO CHANGES THAT HAD TO SHIP TOGETHER. (1) THE LADDER. lib/registry/links.ts returns an ordered list - agenda, meeting record, all-agendas portal, body homepage, directions - and OMITS every rung it cannot fill, so an empty ladder is a true statement rather than a cue to invent one. There is deliberately no fallback that constructs a plausible URL from a jurisdiction name; that is the 4.5.3 fabrication in a new costume. Each link carries SOURCED or DERIVED and the type enforces it: the only DERIVED rung is the OpenStreetMap directions link built from coordinates we already sourced, and it renders with a derived tag so it can never be read as a citation sitting among real ones. OpenStreetMap chosen because it needs no key and no account, so nothing about the reader is traded for the link, and because CLAUDE.md rules out Google Maps. The venue address in meeting-panel.tsx is no longer inert either. (2) THE AUDIT, 4.6.1. lib/registry/audit.ts plus a hand-curated lib/registry/coverage-audit.ts, cited the way lib/sources/legistar/clients.ts is. CoverageStatus gained NOT_ATTEMPTED and SOURCE_BLOCKED, and NO_SOURCE_FOUND STOPPED BEING THE DERIVATION DEFAULT - it is now a claim that requires an audit row recording an exhausted hunt. The registry currently reports 258 NOT_ATTEMPTED, 6 KNOWN_UNCOVERED, 1 SOURCE_BLOCKED and ZERO NO_SOURCE_FOUND, which is the honest picture and was previously 265 rows all reading NO_SOURCE_FOUND alike. Seven real hunts are recorded with every rung they walked, including the misses. build-registry.ts overlays the audit and THROWS on an audit row whose bodyId matches no body, since a stale identifier would otherwise leave a body looking unlooked-at forever. What the overlay deliberately does NOT touch is bodyOrigin, name, sourceDataset and provenance - the first attempt set bodyOrigin to SOURCED and tests/registry-oracle.test.ts caught it: finding a body website does not make the body EXISTENCE a sourced claim, that stays structural and the name stays null on all 265 rows. Three findings came out of the hunts and are on D13, D15 and D21."
